title: "Hands-On: Stash and Switch"

# Hands-On: Stash, Work on Another Branch, Apply

Park a README edit, fix a typo on `main`, come back, apply the stash.

```bash
cd ~/desk/desk-api
git switch main
git status
```

## Park work

```bash
echo "TODO: metrics" >> README.md
git stash push -m "metrics todo"
git status
git stash list
```

## Other work

```bash
git switch -c fix/readme-typo
echo "typo-lab $(date -Iseconds)" >> README.md
git add README.md
git commit -m "docs: lab timestamp"
git switch main
git merge --ff-only fix/readme-typo
git branch -d fix/readme-typo
```

## Restore the stash

```bash
git stash list
git stash apply stash@{0}
cat README.md
git add README.md
git commit -m "docs: TODO for metrics"
git stash drop stash@{0}
git stash list
git status
```

If `apply` conflicted, resolve markers, `git add`, commit, then `drop`.

## Tag this point

```bash
git tag -a v0.1.0-lab -m "after stash lab"
git show v0.1.0-lab --quiet
git tag -d v0.1.0-lab
```

## Done when

- `TODO: metrics` is committed on `main`
- `git stash list` is empty (or only older stashes you had before)
- status is clean
